story.title: Hands-on with Apple’s touchscreen MacBook Pro

facts.text: After months of rumors and speculation , Apple just announced its latest entry-level addition to its MacBook lineup: the MacBook Neo.

Priced at $599 and equipped with an A18 processor (the same chip found in the iPhone 16 Pro), Apple takes aim at budget PCs and Chromebooks in the low-end PC market — an area in which it historically has had virtually no market share.
In fact, the Neo, with its current hardware and ecosystem-based software, can give similarly priced Dell, HP, Acer, and other Windows laptops a good run for their money.
Having continuity features with the iPhone, alone, may convinced existing PC users to make the switch.

As the entry-level device in its laptop lineup, Apple’s recently announced MacBook Air M5 and MacBook Pro and Pro Max M5 saw price increases of $100 to $400, pushing those models further into premium territory to make room for the affordable Neo.
Sure, the iMac M4 dropped in a handful of fun colorways, but the laptops specifically have been steadfastly monotone for too long.

This is something Apple used to be known for, after all — lightness and accessibility.
Alongside the teasers, Apple has also sent media invites for an experience in LA on October 28, 2026.
That’s the same wording the company used to describe its ‘Welcome Home’ event, so I’d suspect there won’t be a formal keynote, but there will be plenty of hands-on time.
However, Joswiak’s post teases something Pro that could be on the horizon.
There’s been no shortage of rumors, and it’s likely that Apple will drop a significant update to the MacBook Pro family next week, finally delivering a touchscreen laptop.
Either way, we only have a few more days to wait to see what Apple has been working on.
After all, the company has promised to ‘Pro and Tell.’ Let me know what you’re most excited about in the comments below.
Recent reports also hint that the M6 could be coming to the iMac , which is due for an upgrade after launching with the M4 in 2024.

Both the new 14-inch and 16-inch models are expected to pair the first touchscreen on a Mac with an OLED display, delivering the same vibrant, rich viewing experience as an OLED iPhone or iPad Pro, all within a redesigned, slimmer notebook.
Alongside the Mac, the iPad could also be in the mix, potentially hinted at by the vibrant colors and what appears to be a finer, brush-drawn Apple logo.
Coming shortly after the iPhone Duo starts shipping, a major iPad mini upgrade is also rumored.
Jacob Krol is the US Managing Editor, News for TechRadar.
I’ve been wishing for a redesigned iPad mini with Magic Keyboard support and a better screen for a while, so this would be music to my ears, and likely to many others’ too.
The iPad lineup is still in pretty good shape, with the Air and Pro models already receiving updates with better processors earlier this year.

To me, it looks as though a finger could be drawing the logo, given the overall shape, or perhaps a brush of some sort is being used to create it.
Either way, it points to the likely arrival of new Macs or iPads.

In addition to touchscreen laptops, the anonymous Bloomberg sources said to expect Apple's presentation to include a redesigned iPad Mini with an OLED display, and smaller updates to the entry level 14-inch MacBook Pro and iMac to add the new M6 chip that debuted with the Mac mini refresh .
And that won't be Apple's only set of reveals this month; it's also slated to introduce a new collection of smart home gadgets on October 13.
Rumors about a touchscreen edition of Apple's high-end laptop date back to 2023 .
So, not a 100-percent solid date for a product announcement, but still a more concrete time frame than we've ever had about Apple's long-awaited touchscreen laptop debut.

The new 14-inch MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR display weighs just 3 pounds, which is noticeably lighter than the current generation of non-touch MacBook Pros, which start at 3.4 pounds for the newly introduced M6 models.
Touch works almost exactly like you’d expect it to with Apple’s first-party apps.
Steve Jobs famously called touchscreen laptops “ergonomically terrible,” and for over a decade, Apple stridently refused to make one.
Today that all changes with the MacBook Pro — the company’s first laptop to embrace a touch interface.
While it’s unlikely that Apple can fix all the “terrible” ergonomics of having to lift your arm up and touch a laptop screen, the company has put some effort into making macOS more touch-friendly.
